technical_and_design_decisions: Implement the increment as a standalone Go library package (fabric channel configuration API, i.e., a 'configtx'-style package) that consumes and produces Hyperledger Fabric protobuf messages (common.Config, common.ConfigEnvelope, common.ConfigUpdate, common.ConfigUpdateEnvelope, msp.FabricMSPConfig).

Depend on the hyperledger/fabric proto definitions and use protolator (DeepMarshalJSON/DeepUnmarshalJSON) for lossless JSON<->protobuf conversion of the config tree, mirroring how configtxgen/configtxlator represent channel configuration.

Model the API around a ConfigTx value that holds both the original (read-set) configuration and a working copy (write-set); every mutating function modifies the working copy, and a ComputeUpdate function diffs original vs. modified config groups to produce a common.ConfigUpdate, satisfying the 'multiple changes / state management' requirement in U5.

Provide functional-helpers API surface: New(configEnvelope), AddAnchorPeer, RemoveAnchorPeer, GetAnchorPeers, RevokeCertificate, AddRootCAToMSP, GetOrdererConfiguration, UpdateOrdererConfiguration, NewCreateChannelTx, CreateConfigUpdateEnvelope, and SignConfigUpdate.

Compute the ConfigUpdate by constructing the updated ConfigGroup, then producing read_set/write_set diffs with mod_policy version handling, and wrap the result plus collected signatures into a ConfigUpdateEnvelope ready for the standard signature workflow (no orderer submission in scope).

For U4 certificate validation, parse PEM to x509.Certificate and reject certificates where IsCA is false or KeyUsageCertSign is not set in KeyUsage; do not perform chain-of-trust or expiry validation beyond that minimal check.

For U3, implement revocation by appending the certificate's identifier (PEM string, consistent with Fabric's CRL-based revocation_list entries on FabricMSPConfig) to the target org's MSP revocation_list and bumping MSP/config versions appropriately.

Signing helper uses a local MSP SigningIdentity (serialised identity + private key from the filesystem) to sign the ConfigUpdate bytes and append signatures to the envelope; support accumulating multiple signatures.

Testing strategy: table-driven unit tests per function using fixture config blocks generated by configtxgen (sample two-org + orderer channel), plus runnable GoDoc Example functions (Example*_test.go) for U5-U8 as required.
No new consensus/membership components; purely client-side configuration library targeting the Fabric 1.4/2.x config schema referenced in the user stories.
assumptions: The input to all mutating/retrieval functions is a valid existing channel configuration obtained as a common.Config or common.ConfigEnvelope (e.g., decoded from a config block or fetched config), as stated in the acceptance criteria.
Fabric protobuf dependencies (common, msp, orderer, peer protos) and protolator are already available as importable Go modules; no proto regeneration work is required.

The library only needs to produce signature-ready ConfigUpdateEnvelope / channel-creation transactions; submitting to an orderer, peer CLI integration, and the online signature workflow itself are out of scope.

Test fixtures (sample configtx.yaml and generated config blocks/envelopes) can be produced locally with configtxgen; no permanent live Fabric network is needed, at most a short-lived local smoke-test network.
Revocation in U3 means the Fabric MSP revocation_list mechanism (list of PEM CRL / revoked-certificate identifiers on FabricMSPConfig), not integration with fabric-ca's CRL generation.
The developer is proficient in Go and already familiar with Hyperledger Fabric channel configuration structure; no ramp-up/training time is included.

Estimates cover design, implementation, unit tests, GoDoc examples, integration verification, code review, and documentation polish, but exclude release packaging/publishing, CI pipeline setup beyond a basic build, and long-term maintenance.
Anchor peer add/remove operates on a named org's AnchorPeers value (host/port list) within the application orgs section of the channel config.
Work is performed by a single developer; all estimates are effort (workdays), not calendar time.

activities.activity_description: Create the Go module/repository, wire dependencies on Fabric protos and protolator, set up linting/formatting and a basic build/test workflow, and generate reusable test fixtures (sample channel config block and config envelopes via configtxgen) used by all subsequent tests.

activities.activity_name: Core ConfigTx model and config update computation
activities.activity_description: Implement the core package types and mechanics shared by all user stories: loading a Config/ConfigEnvelope into a ConfigTx struct (original vs. working copy), navigating/modifying the ConfigGroup tree, protolator-based JSON marshal/unmarshal helpers, version and mod_policy handling, and ComputeUpdate that diffs read-set and write-set to emit a common.ConfigUpdate. Includes unit tests.

activities.activity_name: Config update envelope and signing workflow helpers
activities.activity_description: Implement CreateConfigUpdateEnvelope (wrap ConfigUpdate, attach signatures) and SignConfigUpdate (compute signature header from MSP signing identity, sign config update bytes, append ConfigSignature). Supports accumulating multiple signatures for the signature workflow referenced in U1-U5. Includes unit tests.

Implement AddAnchorPeer(configTx, orgName, anchorPeer) that locates the named application org's values, decodes/updates the AnchorPeers value (host, port), re-marshals it into the config group, and bumps versions so a valid ConfigUpdate can be computed. Unit tests verify the resulting ConfigUpdateEnvelope is correct and signature-ready against fixture configs.

Implement RemoveAnchorPeer(configTx, orgName, anchorPeer) mirroring A4: decode the org's AnchorPeers, remove the matching host/port entry, re-marshal, and handle error cases (org not found, anchor peer not present, empty list). Unit tests verify the computed ConfigUpdate.

Implement RevokeCertificate(configTx, orgName, certificate): locate the org's MSP value, unmarshal msp.MSPConfig -> FabricMSPConfig, append the revoked certificate's identifier (PEM) to the revocation_list attribute, re-marshal the nested MSP config into the config group, and handle errors (org/MSP not found, malformed cert). Unit tests assert revocation_list contents and valid ConfigUpdate output.

Implement AddRootCAToMSP(configTx, orgName, caCertPEM): parse the PEM to x509.Certificate, reject certificates missing IsCA/KeyUsageCertSign per acceptance criteria, append the PEM to FabricMSPConfig root_certs, re-marshal, and update versions. Unit tests cover valid CA certs, rejection of non-CA certs, and malformed input.

Implement GetAnchorPeers(configTx, orgName) returning the org's current anchor peers (host/port list) without manual parsing, with appropriate not-found errors. Update the package example test to demonstrate usage of this helper as required by the acceptance criteria.

Implement GetOrdererConfiguration returning a config.Orderer struct (addresses, batch size/timeout, consensus type, kafka/etcdraft metadata, channel restrictions, capabilities) decoded from the orderer config group, and UpdateOrdererConfiguration(configTx, orderer) that writes a modified Orderer back into the config group so users can persist unchanged fields. Update example tests to demonstrate the retrieve-modify-update round trip.

activities.activity_name: U5: GoDoc example - configuration updates with signing
activities.activity_description: Write a runnable GoDoc Example (Example function) demonstrating idiomatic usage: load an existing config, apply multiple sequential changes (e.g., add anchor peer then update orderer value) showing state management across mutations, compute the ConfigUpdate, wrap it in an envelope, and sign it. Verify the example compiles and runs in tests.

activities.activity_name: U6: GoDoc example - channel creation transaction with signing
activities.activity_description: Implement NewCreateChannelTx (build a config template for a new channel and produce a create-channel ConfigUpdateEnvelope) and write a runnable GoDoc Example demonstrating creating and signing a channel creation transaction. Verify the example compiles and runs in tests.

End-to-end verification across all user stories: run the produced ConfigUpdate envelopes through Fabric's own validation path (protolator round-trip and, where feasible, a short-lived local test network or configtxlator checks) to confirm computed updates are accepted as valid; fix defects found.

activities.activity_name: Code review, refactoring, and documentation polish
activities.activity_description: Self-review pass over the full increment: refactor duplicated config-group traversal code, normalize error handling and exported API naming, ensure GoDoc comments and README describe all functions and examples, run full test suite and linters, and prepare the increment for delivery.
